thin_MCP_contract.input_boundary: Exactly one bound sealed original public content array per consumer. Preserve original text string bytes, image base64 string bytes, decoded PNG bytes and dimensions. The JSON-RPC envelope may carry the current request ID. Log original payload SHA and actual RX SHA separately.
thin_MCP_contract.identity_and_access_records: Freeze complete tool schema and per-case public content before the first consumer. Record every request, returned envelope, content hash, text and PNG byte counts, service timing and source-read paths. Keep the scoring endpoint outside the exposed tool surface.
thin_MCP_contract.stdio_protocol: initialize, tools/list, tools/call and ping are sufficient for the existing CLI. Log every input line and preserve JSON-RPC ID types. Notification handling follows the expected stdio protocol. Empty arguments require a literal JSON object with zero members.
thin_MCP_contract.delivery_proof: Compare actual completed CLI MCP image blocks against original PNG SHA and full width/height. Original payload delivery and tool completion are measurable. Provider-internal visual use remains unmeasured.

authentication_and_configuration.current_preflight_pattern: The legacy preparer runs fixed-binary --version and login status with captured output. It records status and output hash and retains zero sensitive output bytes.
authentication_and_configuration.isolation_adaptation: The legacy safe_environment retains CODEX_HOME when present. The new runner can explicitly bind its isolated config/home path and retain login material privately outside the source/archive manifest. CLI arguments supply --ignore-user-config, --ignore-rules and --strict-config. Each independent consumer receives a fresh workspace and no resume ID.

required_adaptation_findings.finding: The inherited event loop hardcodes a twelve-call upper bound. Its private-globals adaptation keeps that literal. Enforce four attempts at the thin server/controller admission point, record every repeated call, and independently validate actual completed and attempted counts.

Recovery qualification sets consumer_deadline equal to the 600-second owned deadline and starts live native/product processes. The current batch contract uses 450-second tasks, 600-second process life and sealed file replay.

The legacy adapter forwards through a held TCP owner and leaves that owner alive on EOF. A direct sealed-content stdio server can keep a single child process. Its STARTED/EXIT receipts and retained-handle closure need qualification through the actual selected entry point.

Read-only CLI settings and disabled tools constrain the exposed interface. The runner must verify actual tools/list, unexpected tool events and actual thin-server file reads. The historical Python/Blender audit hook belongs to execute-code sessions and adds irrelevant live dependencies here.

The result matcher canonicalizes JSON container serialization. Byte-preservation evidence therefore also needs exact original text bytes, original image/base64 strings, decoded PNG SHA and the actual per-call RX payload. Preserve original sealed content fields and order.

Historical thin EXIT receipts can be missing when the CLI closes its MCP client. Preserve that state. Record actual retained-handle exit separately, including the actual exit code, before advancing to the next consumer.

Historical login success and current auth-file existence establish available local configuration paths. Current login validity, Pro quota and real image transfer require the root-owned preflight and actual bounded consumer execution.

new_runner_review.root_followup_required: Apply this report to the root-authored runner, then qualify the selected protocol/event/closure path before actual S1/S2/S3 consumption.
